Lau Ca Keo 2 Revisted
Feb 2015 • Couples
It has been a couple days short of a year, when I last reviewed this restaurant. Unfortunately, I must report this venue is no longer worth a visit in my mind. While it still seemed popular with locals, there appeared to be fewer than before. There also seemed to be fewer tables than before. When we arrived a couple nights ago, we were anxious for the same experience we had last year. Sadly, that wouldn't be.

We arrived shortly after 5 PM, found our own seats and were promptly served with menus. There were fewer items than last year and many of the less expensive ones were off the menu. Still, we found some selections, which appeared to have price increases of more than 30% since last year. Here is a selection of items we ordered:

Ca Loc hap bau- (grilled fish) 99,000d
Mo xao hai san- (stir fried seafood) 99,000d
Tom dat nuong muoi ot- (grilled shrimp) 99,000d
Ngheu Hap- (steamed clams in lemongrass) 89,000d
Com- (rice) 25,000d
Beer- (333) 26,000d

Understanding that prices had increased, we still ordered because the food was quite good last year. My wife was anxious for the grilled fish and rice and not so much for anything else. We fully expected all of the food items to be tabled at the same time but they came out individually with several minutes lapsing between items.

First to the table was 24 itsy-bitsy, steamed clams, so small that all the clams when taken from their shells they only partially filled a very small condiment dish. I mean these were extremely small clams maybe the size of a US dime coin, maybe each 15 mm across. Obviously, it didn’t take long to consume this, which my wife also ate.

Next came the grilled shrimp (with heads on). Once the head was removed and the internals sucked out clean, there wasn't much of a shrimp left to eat after the shells were removed. There were 10 of these shrimp but very small compared to the ones we ate last year and not as good (seemed mushy).

About 10 minutes later, out came some eggs noodles stir fried with four small shrimp, a couple pieces of tough calamari and vegetables. My wife’s fish came out as well all cut up in pieces. My wife asked what it was because it didn’t look like fish. She was told it was frog! Sadly again, there was nothing lost in translation when we ordered because my wife is Vietnamese and ordered all the dishes. The frog was taken away.

About the time I was finishing the mixed seafood hai san, which was really just stir fried egg noodles, we still had not been served the steamed rice. Staff were in disarray and running amok. My wife was extremely upset and took charge. 

She left the table to seek out the owner, which appeared to be absent this year. She told them to cancel the fish, the rice and just paid for what was consumed. A poor service experience at best. At the end of the day, we can no longer recommend eating here. Hopefully, nobody else will either.

Richard

Where the Locals Eat
Mar 2014 • Couples
Lẩu Cá Kèo 2 Tôm Restaurant
11A Tô Hiến Thành Street, Nha Trang
Tel: 01255.000.199

GPS Coordinates: N 12º 14’ 29.9”, E 109º 11’ 32.2”

This is a restaurant where the locals eat. It’s not far from Cho Xom Moi area. It can be reached using the #5 bus or walk if you're staying in the tourist area. When we arrived around 6:15 PM, diners were already seated, so we came none too early. I was the only westerner in the place right up until we left at 7:30 PM. Go where the locals eat so they say, and we weren’t let down. 

The menu is extensive with some English translations that might make you laugh. Not to worry; they have pictures, which do a fair job of what you will be eating. It would be useful to be able to speak a bit of Vietnamese but probably not necessary. The prices were reasonable and we had our fill of many dishes and beers for 316,000d. Here is what we ordered:

1. Soup Hai San (Seafood Soup), two bowls - 38,000d
2. Steamed rice, one plate (enough for two) - 8,000d
3. Nghau Hap Thai (Thai style steamed clams) - 59,000d
4. Rau Muong Xao Toi (On choy) - 39,000d
5. Tom Nuong Muoi Ot, (Grilled Shrimp with salt & chili, about 10 med. shrimp) - 69,000d
6. Ca Loc Nuong Trui (Grilled Snakehead fish) with rice papers and herbs - 79,000d
7. Saigon Red beer, two bottles - 24,000d

We left the table absolutely stuffed but not before congratulating the owner on a job well done.

Now my wife said the Hai San soup had a bit too much cornstarch in it (thickening powder) but I though it was about right. Also, it wasn’t salty so I added a bit of soy sauce. The steamed rice was a big enough serving for two. The shellfish, including the steamed clams and grilled shrimped were cooked right, not too long and tasted quite fresh. 

One other note is that the grilled fish comes with rice papers and herbs, which is additional but the menu doesn’t indicate such. For some reason, they expected that we wanted the herbs and the rice papers to roll the fish in but we didn’t. They charge less than 20,000d if you want the rice papers and herbs. Make sure you let them know you don’t want it as the menu doesn’t indicate. It was deleted from out bill.

As for atmosphere, this is where locals come to eat. It's not romantic but it serves great food. Lots of families with kids were eating here, and one toddler was screaming like crazy.
